3.speaker: Manus Sazon
3.text: "The first item on our agenda concerns the war with Pales."

4.speaker: Daria de Rava
4.text: "The first item on our agenda concerns the war with Pales."

5.speaker: Manus Sazon
5.text: "I must state that my party harbors reservations about the current conflict. As do many Rizian citizens."

9.speaker: Manus Sazon
9.text: "They are suspicious of the motives for our invasion, and fear a repeat of the 1920s."

10.speaker: Manus Sazon
10.text: "Though our invasion could be seen as justified, many fear a repeat of the 1920s."

11.speaker: Daria de Rava
11.text: "Objection. His Majesty's decision to go to war was made in full accordance with the Royal Council, and is not up for discussion today."

12.speaker: Manus Sazon
12.text: "I am not contesting the King's decision. Merely reflecting the point of view of his subjects."

13.speaker: Player_Romus
13.text: "I did not want to go to war myself. But I did what I had to for the good of my kingdom."

17.speaker: Manus Sazon
17.text: "While the King's intention to reclaim Rizia's lost territory was well-received at his coronation, the temperature in this country has changed. As has the international climate."

18.speaker: Manus Sazon
18.text: "It is difficult for my party to support an all-out attack on the Grand Duchy, especially when the future of Zille is still in doubt."

19.speaker: Manus Sazon
19.text: "At the beginning of his reign, His Majesty hinted he would take a conciliatory approach towards international politics. Unfortunately, that no longer appears to be true."

23.speaker: Manus Sazon
23.text: "While some Rizians do still hold out hope for the annexation of Pales, the temperature in this country has changed. As has the international climate."

24.speaker: Daria de Rava
24.text: "Needless to say, we in the RNC stand fully behind our troops, as does the rest of the country."

26.speaker: Player_Romus
26.text: "And your subjects would rather we roll over in submission to the Palesians and their greedy puppetmasters?"

27.speaker: Player_Romus
27.text: "If I am sending my people to fight for a cause they do not fully believe in, that's indeed troubling."

30.speaker: Manus Sazon
30.text: "There must surely have been a middle ground between that and outright war. But it is now too late to find it."

31.speaker: Daria de Rava
31.text: "Your concern is valid, Mr. Sazon, but the tax your party is proposing will only damage Rizia's wartime morale, not boost it."

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: Several yellow-sashed representatives from Cardesse-Montaklar immediately stood up in objection.

35.speaker: Manus Sazon
35.text: "In this way, we can ensure continued funding for our domestic programs, including care for our veterans, in spite of the heavy costs of the war effort."

36.speaker: Daria de Rava
36.text: "Even if we needed the money... these are the same industries that have been working tirelessly to supply our troops with weapons and equipment. They should be lauded, not penalized."

37.speaker: Daria de Rava
37.text: "Keep in mind that these are the same industries that have been working tirelessly to supply our troops with weapons and equipment. They should be lauded, not penalized."

38.speaker: Manus Sazon
38.text: "As I was saying. Now that we are engaged in this unfortunate conflict, measures must be taken to mitigate its impact on ordinary citizens."

39.speaker: Manus Sazon
39.text: "If we are to remain engaged in this unfortunate conflict, measures must be taken to mitigate its impact on ordinary citizens."

40.speaker: Manus Sazon
40.text: "It is a simple fact that war is a source of suffering for many and enormous financial windfalls for an elite few."

41.speaker: Manus Sazon
41.text: "In the name of equity, the RPP is proposing an excess profits tax on the businesses and industries that stand to generate the most revenue from the Pales campaign."

45.speaker: Daria de Rava
45.text: "With all due respect, Mr. Sazon, what you're proposing is utterly unnecessary. Rizia can fund both its internal programs and the military without going into the red."

46.speaker: Daria de Rava
46.text: "There have been some isolated anti-war protests at universities, particularly in Brenas. But those do not represent the general opinion of the Rizian populace."

47.speaker: Manus Sazon
47.text: "Objection. Madame Speaker is downplaying the amount of opposition to the Pales conflict."

51.speaker: Manus Sazon
51.text: "A great many citizens are suspicious of the motives for our invasion, and fear a repeat of the 1920s."

52.speaker: Manus Sazon
52.text: "Though Pales seems to have been the instigator this time around, a great many citizens fear a repeat of the 1920s."

53.speaker: Manus Sazon
53.text: "It is difficult for the RPP to support an all-out attack on the Grand Duchy, especially when the future of Zille is still in doubt."

54.speaker: Daria de Rava
54.text: "Nobody is asking your party to support the war. We only ask you to respect the will of the majority of citizens who do."

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "I am receptive to your concerns, Mr. Sazon. But what's done is done. We are at war whether we like it or not."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "On the contrary, Madame Speaker, the members of the RPP *will* support the war or face the consequences."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "Are you forgetting they have taken my daughter hostage? Would you rather I leave her to die?"

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "Precisely. Do not fool yourself into thinking a few fringe movements represent the masses."

62.speaker: Manus Sazon
62.text: "Regardless of how many Rizians support the military operation, we can all agree that it will take an enormous amount of resources."

66.speaker: Manus Sazon
66.text: "We will support the war if we can find a way to mitigate its impact on our internal welfare."

67.speaker: Manus Sazon
67.text: "Which brings me to the proposal I submitted--"

68.speaker: Manus Sazon
68.text: "Yes, I agree. Which is why we must take steps to mitigate the conflict's impact on ordinary citizens."

70.speaker: Daria de Rava
70.text: "Yes, Mr. Sazon. We were getting to that."

71.speaker: Manus Sazon
71.text: "Of course not, Your Majesty. Her Highness' return is of the utmost priority."

73.speaker: Manus Sazon
73.text: "Of course not, Your Majesty. Everyone in this room knows how much Her Highness means to me."

78.speaker: Manus Sazon
78.text: "At the same time, we cannot ignore the impact the war will have on ordinary citizens."

79.speaker: Daria de Rava
79.text: "To generate funding for domestic programs during wartime, the Rizian People's Party has proposed a 'war profits tax' on those very same businesses and industries that are working tirelessly to equip our troops."

80.speaker: Manus Sazon
80.text: "Such as what, Ms. de Rava? Your party refused to consider the RPP's inheritance and landowner tax proposals. Is your only solution to place the burden on those who can least afford it?"

81.speaker: Player_Romus
81.text: "I agree. We are relying on these companies to help win the war. To levy unfair taxes upon them would be to bite the hand that feeds us."

82.speaker: Player_Romus
82.text: "If our business owners truly support Rizia, they will do their part to keep the rest of the kingdom afloat during these difficult times."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "That income they're making is blood money. If they have any sort of conscience, they won't want to keep it."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "You will refrain from commenting out of turn, Madam *Minority* Speaker."

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: Next to me, Hugo spoke through gritted teeth.

86.speaker: Daria de Rava
86.text: "I am sorry. But it's important that you get the full picture."

87.speaker: Daria de Rava
87.text: "Precisely. If we need to pad out our budget, there are other ways to go about it."

91.speaker: Daria de Rava
91.text: "Your Majesty, the RNC does not condone this decree at all."

92.speaker: Hugo Toras
92.text: "Your Majesty, this tax would disproportionately affect House Azaro, as well as the de Ravas themselves. I don't think it's a good idea."

93.speaker: Manus Sazon
93.text: "The full picture is that if Rizia fails its citizens, we will have nobody willing to fight our wars."

97.speaker: Daria de Rava
97.text: "I do not dispute that we all must make sacrifices in times of war. But this particular one could severely hinder our chances of victory."

98.speaker: Manus Sazon
98.text: "Ms. de Rava, I know you are used to being in charge of these proceedings, but I beg you to remember that is no longer the case."

108.speaker: Manus Sazon
108.text: "Such as what, Ms. de Rava? Your party issued an official disproval of His Majesty's landowner tax decree. Is your only solution to place the burden on those who can least afford it?"

111.speaker: Manus Sazon
111.text: "The House of Delegates supports this proposal by a high margin. Therefore, it will be passed on to the King to enact as he sees fit."

112.speaker: Manus Sazon
112.text: "Ms. de Rava's party issued an official disproval of His Majesty's inheritance tax decree. Her preferred solution, it seems, is to place the burden on those who can least afford it."

114.speaker: Daria de Rava
114.text: "According to the latest treasury numbers from Councilor Werner, Rizia can fund both its internal programs and the military without going into the red."

115.speaker: Player_Romus
115.text: "You will refrain from commenting out of turn, Mr. Sazon."

116.speaker: Manus Sazon
116.text: "I'm sorry. But I wanted you to get the full picture."

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "We are relying on these companies to help win the war. To levy unfair taxes upon them would be to bite the hand that feeds us."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "That income they're making is blood money. If they have any sort of conscience, they won't want to keep it."

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: Manus nodded. Next to me, Hugo spoke through gritted teeth.

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "If our business owners truly support Rizia, they will do their part to keep the rest of the kingdom afloat."

122.speaker: Hugo Toras
122.text: "Your Majesty, this tax would disproportionately affect House Azaro, as well as the de Ravas themselves. I don't think it's a good idea."

123.speaker: Daria de Rava
123.text: "I do not dispute that fighting for our country requires sacrifice. But this particular one could severely hinder our chances of victory."

124.speaker: Daria de Rava
124.text: "The full picture is that if we punish the companies responsible for our national defense, we will lose this war even worse than the last one."

126.speaker: Daria de Rava
126.text: "The House of Delegates has already voted down this proposal by a high margin. We recommend that the King ignore it."

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "Sensible. No need for it to go any further."

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: She turned a page in her binder.

129.speaker: Daria de Rava
129.text: "Certainly, Your Majesty. I'll make sure it reaches your desk."

132.speaker: Manus Sazon
132.text: "I had hoped you would at least allow it to reach your desk. But as you wish."

133.speaker: Manus Sazon
133.text: "I had hoped it would go through some sort of legislative process. But good news regardless."

134.speaker: Player_Romus
134.text: "Send it to me regardless. I will decide what to do with it later."

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "I'm afraid I have to go against your recommendation. Rizia will implement the war profits tax that the RPP proposed." [-3 Authority]

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "Very good. My Grand Vizier will make sure it crosses my desk. Won't you, Your Grace?"

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "No need, Mr. Speaker. I have no interest in passing such a decree."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "Why go through all that trouble? I'll sign the war profits tax decree immediately."

145.speaker: Daria de Rava
145.text: "If we need funding, we can get it another way. The companies in question should be lauded for their contribution to the cause, not penalized."

146.speaker: Daria de Rava
146.text: "And even if that wasn't the case, the companies in question should be lauded for their contribution to the cause, not penalized."

147.speaker: Manus Sazon
147.text: "You are misrepresenting our proposal, Madam Speaker."

148.speaker: Manus Sazon
148.text: "It is an undeniable fact that war is a source of suffering for many and enormous financial windfalls for an elite few."

149.speaker: Manus Sazon
149.text: "What we are proposing is a move towards equity. It is not fair that our military operation will put a strain on social welfare while fattening the pockets of weapons executives."

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: Manus turned a page in his binder.

158.speaker: Manus Sazon
158.text: "The next item is an update on our progress with Zille."

159.speaker: Daria de Rava
159.text: "The next item is an update on our progress with Zille."

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: "Mr. Sazon, I am confident that our victory in Pales will be swift enough that such a measure will not be called for."

164.speaker: Manus Sazon
164.text: "I hope so as well. But I will send you the proposal in case you choose to enact it in the future."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "I am confident that our victory in Pales will be swift enough that such a measure will not be called for."

170.speaker: Manus Sazon
170.text: "Ms. de Rava's party issued an official disproval of His Majesty's landowner and inheritance tax decrees. Her preferred solution, it seems, is to place the burden on those who can least afford it."
